prompt:
A single flat sheet of SIX separate game-asset paintings arranged in a strict 3-column by 2-row grid, evenly spaced, each object fully inside its own cell with clear empty margin around it and no object touching or overlapping another. Read the cells left to right, top row first.

STYLE, and this is the most important instruction: hand-painted 2D storybook nautical illustration, exactly matching the reference images supplied. Confident dark warm-brown ink linework of varying weight drawn over soft watercolour washes, with visible paper grain and brush texture inside the shapes. Warm timber browns, cream plaster, muted slate-blue and soft sage accents. Slightly wonky hand-drawn geometry, no ruler-straight edges. This is a PAINTING, not a render: no 3D shading, no airbrush gradients, no baked ambient occlusion, no glossy specular highlights, no plastic sheen.

CAMERA, identical for all six cells: three-quarter view from slightly above, each building rotated about thirty degrees so its front face and its left-hand side are both visible, viewed from roughly twenty-five degrees above the ground line. Every building sits at the same angle, the same orientation and the same apparent scale within its cell, so the six read as one set photographed the same way. The footprint of each building sits on an implied ground line at the same height in every cell.

LIGHT, identical for all six: a single warm sun from the upper left, cool soft fill from the upper right, warm interior light glowing through any lit window.

The six are one building upgraded five times: the SAME crew bunkhouse, growing and getting richer, keeping its silhouette family so the change reads as the same place improved rather than six different buildings.

Cell 1, Driftwood Hall: a tiny one-room bunkhouse cobbled from grey salvaged driftwood planks of mismatched widths, a patched canvas roof weighted with stones, one crooked shuttered window, a rough plank door, a coil of rope by the step. Poor, weathered, but swept and cared for.

Cell 2, Oakhewn Hall: the same hut rebuilt properly in squared honey-oak beams, a neat wooden shingle roof, two shuttered windows with warm light behind one, a flat stone doorstep, a small chimney with a thread of smoke.

Cell 3, Brassbound Hall: two storeys now, oak frame with cream plaster panels between the timbers, a brass ship's bell mounted beside the door, brass door bands and brass window latches, three lit windows, a hanging lantern.

Cell 4, Gilded Hall: larger and prouder, gold leaf along the eaves and around the window frames, a carved and gilded crest above the doors, a low balcony, five warmly lit windows, a small flag on a pole.

Cell 5, Hall of Legends: a grand timber hall with a tall gabled roof, long banners hanging either side of double doors, a row of carved ship figureheads set along the facade like statues, tall arched windows glowing amber.

Cell 6, Leviathan Hall: monumental, built around enormous pale whale-bone ribs that arch up over a deep blue-green slate roof, a great leviathan skull mounted as a crest above the doors, bone-carved pillars, windows glowing a warm gold against all that cold bone.

ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT. Do not write the name of any building. Do not put a caption, a label, a title or a number under, over or beside any cell. There is no writing anywhere on this sheet.

ABSOLUTELY NO SUN AND NO GLOW. Do not draw the light source. Do not draw a sun, a moon, a halo, a lens flare, a glow, a radial gradient or any bright disc in any cell. The light comes from off the sheet and is only visible in how the buildings are lit.

BACKGROUND: every cell sits on the SAME FLAT PURE MAGENTA field, RGB 255 0 255, edge to edge across the whole sheet. No ground, no grass, no water, no scenery, no cast shadow on the magenta, no cell borders, no frames, no grid lines, no labels, no text, no numbers, no watermark. The magenta must be completely flat and uniform everywhere the buildings are not.
